title: TBD Loadout Export
description: Loadout download consumed by the mod equip path, in one of two envelope versions. v1 is ACE-shaped: a fixed set of gear slots. v2 is Reforger-shaped: `wear` is an open map keyed by engine LoadoutSlotInfo name (the canonical keys are documented; mod-added areas are allowed), weapons are slot-indexed (two untyped primary slots plus secondary and grenade/throwable, per `Character_Base.et`), and `equipment` / `cargo` are forward skeletons. A v2 envelope also carries a derived legacy `gear` block so a v1 reader keeps working: Enfusion's `JsonLoadContext` ignores unknown fields, so a v1 reader skips the v2 keys instead of failing on them.

wear.description: Wear areas keyed by engine LoadoutSlotInfo name. Canonical keys: headCover, jacket, pants, boots, vest, armoredVest, backpack, handwear (Character_Base.et); pattern-open so mod-added LoadoutAreaType subclasses are representable without a schema change.

weapons.description: Slot-indexed weapons. On vanilla characters slotIndex 0 and 1 are slotType 'primary' (two untyped long slots, so two rifles are legal), 2 is 'secondary' (pistol), 3 is 'grenade' and 4 is 'throwable'. A reader equips through slot-indexed `SetWeapon` rather than a blind `EquipWeapon`, so the authored slot survives.

equipment.description: Equipment micro-slots (SCR_EquipmentStorageComponent): binoculars, wristwatch, … Skeleton in v2 — UI lands with the equipment slice.

cargo.description: Container cargo (volume/weight budget model — no grid cells). Skeleton in v2 — UI and budget validation land with the cargo slice.

cargoContainer.description: Worn container a cargo row is inserted into. Closed vocabulary, kept byte-identical to `mission.schema.json#/$defs/cargoContainer` — this file is the editor-side export and that one is the game-server contract, and the two drifting is exactly the failure the duplication exists to stop. The four keys are fixed by the engine's worn-garment areas (`TBD_LoadoutEquipHelper.GarmentForContainer`) and mirrored by the Arsenal UI's cargo-container list. `armoredVest` is not a key of its own — it shares the vest container.

slot.description: Enfusion ResourceName for the equipped item, or null when the slot is empty.

gear.description: v1 fixed gear slots. In a v2 envelope this block is derived from the v2 fields (jacket → uniform, armoredVest else vest → vest, headCover → helmet, weapons[0] → primary/optic/magazine) so that a v1 reader still works; a v2 reader takes the v2 fields directly.
